Distinct from benchmarks.generated.json (which is per-commit TIMING, all environment=indicative on the dev work-box). Every record here is a DETERMINISTIC, machine-INDEPENDENT metric (recall floor / answer-safety invariant / cost-model crossover / conformance ratchet floor) lifted from a real test or the central conformance scoreboard, so environment=canonical. The honesty gate in scripts/build-papers.mjs FAILS the build if a paper-bound headline table references an environment=indicative record. To add a number a paper may cite as a headline, it MUST appear here as environment=canonical and trace to a named test or const (the `source` field).

filtered_ann.recall_at_10_floor.note: Asserted floor: filtered-traversal recall@10 vs the EXACT-filtered ground truth (nearest_exact_filtered) is gated >= 0.90 on a 20k synthetic set under a ~50% mask. Machine-independent (a deterministic seed + an assertion threshold), not a timing.

ann.recall_at_10_floor.note: Asserted floor: unfiltered HNSW recall@10 vs exact brute force is gated >= 0.95 on a 50k random set. The underlying ANN machinery is unmodified prior art; this floor bounds the approximation the filter operates over.

filtered_ann.prefilter_equals_postfilter.note: Proven by assert_eq: the filtered top-k is byte-identical (same ids, same order) to post-filtering the unfiltered top-k by the same BGP constraint, and is a subset of the unfiltered top-k. This is the answer-safety claim: pre-filtering narrows, never widens, and never changes the answer.

filtered_ann.transitive_equals_postfilte.note: A multi-hop constraint (?node :owns ?x . ?x a :Vehicle) restricts ?node to the projection of the join-connected sub-BGP and matches post-filtering the unfiltered top-k by that same transitive constraint; a disconnected pattern does not affect the mask.

filtered_ann.cyclic_equals_postfilter.note: Connected-component mask derivation terminates (fixpoint worklist) and stays answer-equal to post-filter even when the constraining sub-BGP contains a cycle (?node :owns ?x . ?x :ownedBy ?node).

filtered_ann.prefilter_crossover.note: Deterministic decision rule (not a measured latency): pre-filter is chosen iff m*scatter_penalty <= n, i.e. with the default scatter_penalty 2.0, iff the mask admits <= half the store. Whichever branch is picked the returned top-k is identical, so a mis-estimate costs throughput, never correctness.

policy_bridge.deny_overrides_correct.note: Proven by assertion: when a matched ODRL Permission and a matched ODRL Prohibition both apply to the same principal, action, and target, the materialised deny carved into the auth view wins through the unchanged enforcement layer (which computes union-of-allow minus union-of-deny), so the principal's accessible set for that mode is empty. This realises ODRL's `prohibit` conflict strategy structurally (the bridge re-uses the existing access-control engine rather than adding one); note the bridge does NOT consult `odrl:conflict` — per ODRL IM 2.2 the default when the property is unset is `invalid`, and the `perm`/`invalid` strategies are not representable by set subtraction (disclosed as a first-class limitation in the paper). A deterministic boolean invariant, not a timing, and not a security claim about the wider system.

policy_bridge.fail_closed_deny_retractio.note: Proven by assertion on the refresh path: a materialised deny is retracted only when re-evaluation proves the underlying prohibition is definitely withdrawn; an ambiguous (unprovable) re-evaluation KEEPS the deny so access is never silently widened on uncertainty. This asymmetric, fail-closed retraction rule (three-valued: Applies / Ambiguous / Withdrawn) is a deterministic boolean invariant, not a timing.

policy_bridge.conditional_grant_rechecke.note: Proven by assertion: a faithfully-mappable ODRL recipient constraint is persisted as an ACP conditional grant that is re-checked per session, so only the named recipient is granted (and the materialising party is not auto-granted). An unmappable constraint (for example a purpose constraint) falls back to a one-shot evaluation rather than being mis-encoded as a re-checked condition. A deterministic boolean invariant, not a timing.

policy_bridge.count_enforcement_atomic.note: Proven by assertion behind the opt-in count-enforcement feature: a stateful odrl:count constraint grants exactly up to its limit and then denies, consuming exactly one unit of budget per grant and zero on a denial, with budgets isolated per (rule, party, target). A deterministic boolean invariant over an integer counter, not a timing.
